mechanism_narrative: A persistent rebound in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday trip chains and lunchtime errands, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not stay above its last-4-week mean and RETAIL_REC is not higher in the next 28 days than in the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL time rises while TRANSIT remains depressed, discretionary out-of-home shopping shifts back toward nearby retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above baseline and TRANSIT below baseline in the same week
failure_condition: If a week with RESIDENTIAL above 0 and TRANSIT below 0 is followed by no rise in RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in WORKPLACES mobility signals lost commuting and lunch demand, so retail and recreation weakens over the following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -10.4 at t-2w to -33.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If a week-on-week WORKPLACES drop larger than 10 points is not followed by lower RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM alongside weak PARKS indicates precautionary, necessity-oriented trips rather than discretionary outings, which suppresses retail recreation over the next month.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while PARKS remains below baseline but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A contemporaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies looser access constraints and more downtown circulation, which increases retail recreation with a two-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both cross above their 4-week averages
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both move above their recent 4-week means but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is unusually weak for several weeks, outdoor leisure demand is likely being displaced from public venues, leading to lower retail recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below baseline for four consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift where TRANSIT drops sharply while RESIDENTIAL rises marks substitution from shared transport to staying home, which reduces retail trips over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -5 while RESIDENTIAL rises above +5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -1.0 at t-2w to -10.7 at t-1w while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive
failure_condition: If the TRANSIT-down/RESIDENTIAL-up regime occurs and RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays strongly positive while RETAIL_REC remains below baseline, the area is in a necessity-first pattern that can precede a delayed retail rebound once routine shopping normalizes after four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +20 for at least two weeks
failure_condition: If sustained GROCERY_PHARM above +20 is followed by no improvement in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.
